players.product: intismeran autogene (V940/mRNA-4157) individualized neoantigen therapy, jointly developed with Merck

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K fiscal 2025 costs: cost of sales was $868 million, or 48% of net product sales, including third-party royalties of $88 million, inventory write-downs of $291 million (primarily raw materials and finished and semi-finished COVID vaccine inventory) and unutilized manufacturing capacity and wind-down costs of $93 million; research and development expenses were $3,132 million (-31%) and the net loss was $2,822 million. Inventory on hand was $267 million at December 31, 2025; shelf life is nine to twelve months for Spikevax, twelve months for mNEXSPIKE and eighteen months for mRESVIA.
quarterly_data.figure: cost of sales $868 million (48% of net product sales); inventory write-downs $291 million; unutilized capacity and wind-down $93 million; R&D $3,132 million; net loss $2,822 million

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K manufacturing and supply: at the commercial stage Moderna manufactures drug substance and drug product in collaboration with contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs) in the United States and internationally, depends on single-source suppliers for some components and materials, and has entered non-cancellable or take-or-pay purchase commitments for long-lead raw materials. As of December 31, 2025 it had $411 million of non-cancelable purchase commitments related to raw materials and manufacturing agreements, expected to be paid through 2029. Purchases of property, plant and equipment were $192 million in 2025 versus $1,051 million in 2024.
quarterly_data.figure: $411 million raw-material and manufacturing purchase commitments through 2029; capex $192 million (2024: $1,051 million)

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K: in December 2025 Moderna entered an agreement with the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), which will provide up to $54 million to fund a pivotal Phase 3 trial of its mRNA-based H5 pandemic influenza vaccine candidate mRNA-1018, expected to begin in early 2026; if licensure is granted and a pandemic occurs, Moderna will allocate 20% of its H5 pandemic vaccine manufacturing capacity to low- and middle-income countries.
quarterly_data.figure: up to $54 million CEPI funding; 20% of H5 pandemic vaccine manufacturing capacity

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K: Moderna began a collaboration with OpenAI in early 2023 and in 2024 deployed ChatGPT Enterprise across the company; GPTs are embedded across its legal, research, manufacturing and commercial functions (for example a Dose ID GPT used to evaluate vaccine dose selection).

10-K litigation: in January 2026 Bayer CropScience LLC, Monsanto Company and Monsanto Technology, LLC filed a complaint in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware asserting that Moderna's manufacture and sale of its COVID vaccines infringe a U.S. patent directed to methods of modifying gene sequences; the complaint seeks unspecified damages.

connects_to.relationship: PCV collaboration and license agreement for intismeran autogene (mRNA-4157): Moderna designs and manufactures intismeran and provides manufacturing capacity

contracts.signal: Under the PCV collaboration and license agreement (June 2016, amended 2018), Moderna received a $200 million upfront payment from Merck and was responsible for designing and researching intismeran, providing manufacturing capacity and manufacturing intismeran, and conducting Phase 1 and Phase 2 trials alone and in combination with KEYTRUDA.

connects_to.relationship: mRNA discovery and exclusive mRNA manufacturing for Vertex's cystic fibrosis program (mRNA-3692/VX-522)

contracts.signal: Under the Vertex Agreement (July 2016, amended July 2019) for cystic fibrosis mRNA medicines, Moderna leads discovery during an initial research period and exclusively manufactures (or has manufactured) mRNA for preclinical, clinical and commercialization purposes, subject to Vertex's back-up supply rights, while Vertex runs development and commercialization. Collaboration revenue from Vertex was $13 million in 2025 ($23 million in 2024, $82 million in 2023). The FDA has granted VX-522 Fast Track designation.
